description:
Guard-clause dispatch does not narrow return type per-callsite (unlike plain-pattern dispatch).

DIAGNOSED (2026-07-03, audit-confirmed at f067b8874; NOT a point fix — architectural). Fixture guard_partition_selects_refined_clause: pick({:ok,x}) when positive(x) returns x's refined value; pick({:ok,_}) -> :fallback. main/0 SHOULD return {int, :fallback}; ACTUALLY {int | :fallback, int | :fallback}.

ROOT CAUSE (proven, audit-verified independently): ActivationKey::from_inputs (identity.rs:98) keys purely on argument Ty via address_inputs. Types::int_lit (types/mod.rs:360) DELIBERATELY collapses every numeric literal to plain int ("numeric literals are VALUES, not types... the lattice deliberately cannot express a numeric singleton" — explicit documented design; as_int_singleton at types/mod.rs:980 is a permanent stub returning None). So pick({:ok,1}) and pick({:ok,0}) mint the IDENTICAL ActivationKey, share ONE reachable_clause_ids computation and ONE joined ReturnType fact, read by BOTH call sites in main. Region::Guard correctly returns 'both branches possible' for a genuinely-polymorphic activation — the real problem is that literal identity is erased BEFORE reachability analysis ever runs. Contrast the ATOM case (direct_calls_specialize_atom_pattern_dispatch_by_input): atom_lit singletons SURVIVE into the lattice and genuinely mint distinct activations, so per-callsite narrowing works there.

WHY NOT A POINT FIX: fixing this needs a literal-value channel INDEPENDENT of Ty (e.g. per-callsite guard re-evaluation against the caller's own literal operands, or carrying literal values in the ActivationKey/dispatch input alongside the erased Ty) — a deliberate change to the activation-identity model, not a local dispatch tweak. It is the numeric-literal analogue of what atom singletons already get.

SEQUENCING/RELATION: distinct root from fz-go4.37 (map dead-clause leak, FIXED — that was branch_possible's MapKeyPresent hardcoded true; this is literal erasure at activation identity). Consider alongside any work on ActivationKey/dispatch-input identity. The guard TODO in port_type_infer_test.rs carries the root-cause trace for whoever picks this up; fill it with {int, :fallback} once fixed.
title: Guard-clause dispatch does not narrow return type per-callsite (unlike plain-pattern dispatch)
